_comment: EXAMPLE ONLY - this is a shape reference, not content. The band edges and the two fixed
encounters below exist to show one of each schema feature; the trainer ids name NOTHING and
are not meant to. Which trainers a run fights, and where they sit, is server content (plan
§2.7 keeps a transcribed roster out of the mod entirely), so no roster ships loaded.
Write your own at data/<your-namespace>/roguelite/trainer_rosters/<name>.json, or shadow this
path from your own datapack to delete this example. ops/gen_roguelite_roster.py generates and
validates these files without booting a server, and can cross-check the ids against an RCT
trainer datapack - which this mod cannot do, since it never sees RCT's registry.
A roster holds trainer IDS ONLY. No teams, no species, no levels: teams are authored as RCT
trainers in their own datapack, and the level comes from the wave curve at battle start.
Any field whose name starts with '_' is ignored, which is where comments go. Every other
unknown field is an error, so a typo is reported instead of silently taking a default.
_authored_for: The schedule this roster's coverage is checked against. Optional - these ARE the defaults, and
are spelled out here only because the block is easy to miss. Change them if your run config
differs, or the loader will report holes for waves you will never reach (or miss real ones).
_bands: Bands are NOT about levels - level scaling is applied to whatever trainer turns up. They exist
because scaling a team's level does not scale its MOVES, EVs or held items, so a team authored
for wave 10 fights like a wave-10 team at wave 150 no matter what level it arrives at.
Trainer bands and boss bands are checked separately, and each set must cover every wave of its
kind in 1..run_length with no gaps and no overlaps. A trainer is drawn from the covering band's
pool by a seeded draw on (run seed, wave), so a resumed run meets the same trainer.
EDITING A POOL RE-POINTS RUNS ALREADY IN PROGRESS, appending included - the draw is scaled by
the pool size, so adding a trainer moves which one some later wave of an existing run will
meet. It does not break those runs; they stay deterministic, they just answer from the new
pool. Listing an id twice doubles its share - that is the only weighting mechanism, and the
absence of a weight field is deliberate.

bands._max_wave: Omitted, so this band is open-ended. Level flattens at 100 from about wave 138, so the last band is where difficulty has to come from the team rather than the curve.

_fixed: Fixed encounters beat the bands AND the interval schedule. Two forms, and they mean different
no "kind"  - replace the trainer on a wave that is ALREADY a trainer or boss wave. On a wild
wave it would never fire, so the loader reports it: that is what catches a wave
"kind"     - PROMOTE this wave to a trainer or boss wave and fight this trainer. This is how
a ladder lands on waves the interval cannot reach, and declaring the kind is you
saying you know the wave is not scheduled as one. A promoted wave is not
catchable, and a promotion to boss takes the boss level multiplier.
The two entries below are examples of each form, NOT a schedule. Authoring the schedule is a
content decision and is deliberately left undone.

fixed._note: Wave 50 is already a boss wave, so this only pins WHICH boss.
Wave 182 is a wild wave under 5/10. "kind" promotes it - without that this entry would never fire.
